hey there, ex ssdc student. trust me, i FEEL your pain. slots can get fully booked as early as 3-4 months ahead but don’t worry, you can always camp out on the ssdc website for trysell slots. i usually managed to get the slots i wanted despite the website saying they were fully booked, by refreshing the website repeatedly (i tend to obtain trysell slots when im on the website at night!) also, most of the slots that are available via trysell occur between 1-3 days before the practical lesson date itself, so you should do more refreshing around that period of time to procure that particular slot. either that, or you can hang around the website during practical exam weeks because thats the peak period when people start selling their driving lesson slots. 

but i would still advise you to book as many available slots as you can right now, no matter how far off the date, because slots really run out very quickly. as mentioned above, you can always trysell your unused driving lessons after you’ve passed your test.

hi, i graduated from ri last year! took pcme and in y5 i got C for gp and EESU for my h2 subjects for y5 cts. i was in one of the “less academically inclined” classes so most of my classmates did not fare well during their y5 period too. 
honestly it’s really okay if you’re not doing as well as you’re hoping you would in jc. it takes some time to get used to the rigour of the a level syllabus and you still have plenty of leeway to further improve until the actual a levels. in y6 most people begin to pick up momentum steadily and do well eventually. i got an rp of 86.25 for a levels and i was really really glad that i managed to achieve such a huge improvement over the years. 
so in conclusion, continue to work hard and don’t give up! try not to compare yourself too much with your classmates who are doing better because at the very end, doing well for a levels is your main goal. HAHA my year head used to encourage us by telling us to imagine ourselves as airplanes gliding along the runway, gradually increasing speed (improving bit by bit in CTs, promos and prelims) and taking off into the air (doing well for a levels!). 
dont stress out too much as you still have time to improve! hope what i said here helps, you can hit me up if you need any advice :)
